Was there really a golden age of virtually indestructible appliances?

I think I'd rather pay $4,000 and not think about my washing machine again, than $1,500 and have to do that every 3-10 years. On the bright side, we do get more and more efficient (in theory) every few years.

Indeed there was. My parents still have a working chest freezer from the 50s. Many companies built high quality appliences in the early days of the manufacturing boom only to discover that they wouldn't break, thus presenting issues with future sales and revenues from repairs. Many manufacturers either went out of business or began replacing key parts that were once metal with plastic so that they would experience a higher fail rate and thus drive new sales and repairs. With your washing machine and dryer it's likely the bearings being designed to fail within 3 - 5 years. With your refrigerator it's probably a small part somewhere that was once made of high quality metal and is now created with a more brittle plastic designed to break within a decade or less.
Yes, my granny (Germany) still uses the washing machine she got as a wedding gift in 1947. People were extremely poor back then, but somehow they managed to build these kinds of things.
Ive had some '50s toasters and essentially the only thing to ever break on them is the filament. Just put in a new filament and its as good as new.

Fracking is indeed dangerous. But so is coal mining, oil drilling, nuclear waste, building windmills and solar collectors, and shipping windmills and solar collectors. All energy production poses dangers. Life involves trade-offs. The tradeoffs for natural gas are well worth it. Fracking allows Americans to save money on home heating bills. It's lowered the price of natural gas so much that manufacturing that left America is coming back.

Source : http://mjperry.blogspot.com/2012/03/cheap-nat-gas-brings-manufacturing-back.html

It may make America energy independent. For those concerned about global warming, burning gas instead of oil and coal helps reduce CO2 emissions.

Source : http://www.slate.com/articles/health_and_science/project_syndicate/2012/09/thanks_to_fracking_u_s_carbon_emissions_are_at_the_lowest_levels_in_20_years_.html

So why do someserious people, like Paul Gallay of Riverkeeper, want fracking stopped. This is their case. Gallay cites a study that claims that fracking makes it more likely that you'll have gas (methane) in your tap water.

Source : http://www.propublica.org/documents/item/methane-contamination-of-drinking-water-accompanying-gas-well-drilling

But that study only examined 60 wells. A more recent study looked at 1,700 wells in the same area and found no relation between being close to natural gas drilling and having methane in your water.

Source : http://www.ogj.com/1/vol-109/issue-49/exploration-development/methane-in-pennsylvania-water-full.html

Gallay cites another study by Cornell ecology professor Robert Howarth that says fracking does not reduce greenhouse gas emissions because methane is an unusually powerful greenhouse gas. But an MIT study found that Howarth's estimates of the emissions from fracking are 7 to 30 times too large.

Source : http://m.iopscience.iop.org/1748-9326/7/4/044030/pdf/1748-9326_7_4_044030.pdf

But a study by Cornell scientist Lawrence Cathles also criticizes Howarth's assumptions. (If you want more details, Howarth responded to the critics. Then Cathles responded to the response.)

Fracking opponents also cite accidents like this one: "Frack Fluid Spill in Dimock Contaminates Stream, Killing Fish." An MIT report counted up more cases.

Source : http://www.propublica.org/article/frack-fluid-spill-in-dimock-contaminates-stream-killing-fish-921 Source : http://mitei.mit.edu/system/files/NaturalGas_Appendix2E.pdf

But put that in perspective. There are at least 35,000 active hydraulic fracturing wells in the US. In other words, MIT found about one alleged problem for every 1,000 wells. Mistakes happen; one-per- thousand is about as error-free as energy production gets.

Technology will also make fracking even safer: Scientists recently invented a fracking fluid that is so safe, you can drink it.

Source : http://www.washingtontimes.com/blog/inside-politics/2013/feb/12/colorado-gov-hickenlooper-i-drank-fracking-fluid/

One claim, famously made by the movie Gasland, is that your tap water might catch on fire if you live near a fracking site. Methane is flammable after all, and the film features a man in Colorado whose tap water bursts into flame. So state environmental officials looked in the man's case, and determined that the flammable water was not due to fracking - it was there naturally.

Source : http://cogcc.state.co.us/library/GASLAND%20DOC.pdf

The bottom line is it that fracking brings good things: cheaper energy, jobs, and cleaner air. Even President Obama says that "the natural gas boom has led to cleaner power."

Still, the usual alarmists have already stopped fracking in New York State, Maryland, and Vermont. This won't help the environment. Or poor people.

Fracking does pose risks, but they can be safely managed.

I wouldn't call them a vegan. They'd be someone who eats a plant based diet that also kills fish for their malamute.

I am glad that you're feeding your dog an appropriate diet, since dogs are facultative carnivores and need meat to thrive. I feed my dog a homemade raw and cooked diet and while I haven't used food that was hunted for him, I do buy meat for him. I am still a vegan, as I'd consider you, but I'd call you someone who isn't forcing personal ethics on a dog that is not only incapable of making that decision (and probably wouldn't, in all honesty) but would not do well on a vegetarian diet (certainly never a vegan diet). And I have a lot of respect for that decision.

Now switching to a dog nutrition perspective, fishing yourself might not be the best nutritional option, depending on what you have available to you and where you live. The best fish to feed your dog are the fish that are high in omega-3 but low in mercury, so look for fish that are in the upper right of this chart. Additionally, never ever feed raw fish (salmon, trout, or giant salamander) from the Pacific Northwest, as they are infected with a fluke that can infect and kill a dog or other canids. Also if you do go with fresh fish, I would first deep-freeze the fish for 3-4 weeks to kill off any parasites that the fish might be carrying. However, the safest bet would be to go for canned salmon or canned sardines with no oil or salt added, as they are safe for consumption and the bones are soft enough to feed from the cooking process (also don't feed cooked bones). Like I said, make sure that no oil or salt has been added; the only ingredient should be the fish.

Also check out /v/dogfood if you're interested to learn more! It's a small subverse but I'm hoping we can grow it to be a beneficial resource!
